motivation: Two-slot joint lookahead shows small gains over two-slot additive bids, but an always-up counterexample loses 8 to 6 due to horizon truncation. Compare a stronger established capacity-priced finite-horizon baseline before interpreting this as a new mechanism.
horizon: All visible deadlines, capped at the protocol maximum 8 slots and remaining 32-slot experimental horizon. No unseen future arrivals.
pricing: For each price lambda, solve each destination's exact finite-horizon belief DP with a charge lambda per attempt. Select the price minimizing lambda*K*H + sum(V_i); choose current destinations by active-minus-passive advantage at that price. This is a standard Lagrangian relaxation heuristic, not a proved Whittle index.
uncertainty: Same frozen recurrent CTMC and each policy's own partial feedback as R2. No new fitted parameters; no held-out tuning.
validation: Check the dual bound against exhaustive tiny joint POMDP values, all trace resource/conservation invariants, same all-up negative control, and 1/3/7-day clustered bootstrap sensitivity.
interpretation: Can falsify the R2 apparent improvement. Cannot promote a post-hoc winner as independent confirmation or novelty.
